concepts.title: Classification: Bringing Order to Raw Data
concepts.definition: Raw data, collected unit by unit, is a jumble. Classification arranges it into homogeneous classes on some basis -- geographical, chronological, qualitative or quantitative -- so that the mass can be comprehended and subjected to statistical treatment.
concepts.key_idea: Classification is sorting for sight -- one basis at a time, chaos becomes classes.

solution_steps.explain: Decide the characteristic that matters for the study -- place, time, attribute or variable.
Sort every unit into the class where it belongs, with no overlap and nothing left out.
The classified data is now compact enough for tabulation and statistical analysis.

concepts.title: Variables, Frequency Distributions and Class Intervals
concepts.definition: Quantitative data is organised by variables -- characteristics that take different numerical values. A frequency distribution records how many observations fall into each value or class interval; exclusive classes count values up to the upper limit, inclusive classes include both endpoints, and class marks stand for each interval.
concepts.key_idea: Count the cases per class -- the frequency distribution is the data's first portrait.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest103.txt frequency sections (variables discrete continuous, frequency distribution, exclusive and inclusive classes, class limits class mark tally marks)

solution_steps.explain: Sum the lower and upper limits of the interval.
Half the sum of limits is the class mark representing the whole interval.

concepts.title: Loss of Information and Choice of Classes
concepts.definition: Grouping buys clarity at a price: individual values disappear into intervals, so some information is lost. The statistician must therefore choose the number and width of classes with care -- enough classes to preserve the pattern, few enough to stay readable.
concepts.key_idea: Grouping trades detail for clarity -- the art is losing the least information for the most readability.
concepts.textbook_ref: kest103.txt grouping sections (loss of information, number of classes, width of class intervals, adjusting classes)

solution_steps.explain: Few broad classes are easy to read but blur the distribution's shape; many narrow classes do the reverse.
Choose class limits that are convenient, mutually exclusive and cover the whole range.
Individual identities vanish in grouping, so later exact calculations acknowledge approximation.
